platform_notes: Per our sheets, the Android PAX terminals (A920 Pro, A920 Max, A800, A80, A77, Aries8, Elys) run the BroadPOS payment application with a parameter file built by the processor; other apps arrive from PAXSTORE by serial number, and the Android settings password is separate from the payment app's passwords. The A30, A35 and Q25 are PIN pads driven by a base terminal or POS (BroadPOS / POSDK semi-integration), and the S920 behind the charging base is PAX's traditional, non-Android platform. PAX itself publishes only hardware quick setup guides plus a short FAQ (written around its own payment app's Func/Settings menus, i.e. BroadPOS, without naming it); how to run a sale, refund, void, tip or batch comes from processor/reseller guides, which describe their own builds, so every operation entry carries a note on the application.

entries.title: A920 will not hold a charge (new terminal)
steps: Turn the terminal off.
Remove the battery from the terminal.
Peel the protection sticker off the battery.
Put the battery back in.
Plug in the charger.

entries.title: Apple Pay / contactless is not enabled
steps: Contactless has to be switched on in the terminal's file by the merchant service provider.
After it is enabled, power the terminal off and on so it downloads the change.

entries.title: Attacked
steps: The terminal has detected a hardware security problem and locked itself.
This can happen if the terminal was dropped or tampered with, or if the internal battery is damaged or needs replacing.
It cannot be fixed on site: the terminal must be sent in for repair (RMA).
Stop using the terminal and contact support.
entries.quote: The terminal has detected an insecurity with the hardware and has locked itself in security purposes. This can happen if the terminal was dropped or tampered with. This error message will also appear if the internal battery is damaged or needs to be replaced. With that being said, the machine must be sent to RMA for repair.
entries.note: PAX answers 'Attacked, Triggered, or PED Tampered' as one question.

entries.title: Payment app update is not going through
steps: Close the batch on the terminal: in most cases an update to the payment app is blocked until the batch is closed.
Try the update again.
entries.quote: In most cases the update to payment applications will be blocked unless the batch is closed on the device.
entries.note: Downgrades and firmware updates are covered separately by PAX and need support.

entries.title: Firmware update fails: version jump too large
steps: A firmware update should go to a version close to the current one.
PAX says about 5 to 7 versions ahead is safe; more than that will likely fail.
Firmware updates are done with technical support.
entries.quote: it is safe to jump roughly 5-7 versions ahead of your current but more than that will likely fail.

entries.title: Close the batch
steps: If the terminal is used with a point of sale, close the batch from the POS itself.
On a stand-alone terminal, press Function.
Select Batch.
Select Batch Close.
The terminal prints a batch report if it worked, or shows an error message if it did not.
entries.quote: Press Function -> Select Batch -> Select Batch close -> The terminal will print a batch report if successful or display an error message if unsuccessful.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Tips are not showing correctly
steps: Tips are switched on in the terminal's file build: tips enabled under the EDC tab and Tip 1 enabled under the Tip tab.
The rest depends on how the tips should be configured, so support has to set it.
entries.quote: First make sure you have tips enabled under the EDC tab in your file build.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Password for the payment application
steps: The payment application password is set up by your provider (ISO).
If no custom password was set, it defaults to today's date: two-digit month, two-digit day, four-digit year.
For the Android settings password, contact your provider.
entries.quote: If they have not set a custom password, then it will default to today’s date in a two-digit month, two-digit day and four-digit year format (MM/DD/YYYY).
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Invalid Batch Seq
steps: It means the batch number on the terminal does not match the batch number the processor expects.
Press Function.
Choose Settings.
Choose Host settings.
Choose Batch number.
Increase it by 1 and confirm.
Repeat if the first number does not work.
The processor can also tell you the exact batch number.
entries.quote: “Invalid Batch Sequence” means the batch number on the terminal is not matching the batch number the processor is expecting.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Partial approval: what it is
steps: A partial approval happens when the card does not have enough funds for the full amount, so only the available amount is approved.
Take another form of payment for the difference.
For prepaid gift cards the remaining card balance prints on the receipt.
This is controlled by the host and required by the card brands; it cannot be disabled.
entries.quote: This allows the cardholder to use the card presented for the amount available and for the merchant to obtain an additional form of payment for the difference.

entries.title: Turn off Partial Approval
steps: Partial approval is controlled by the card issuer's bank and cannot be turned off.
The file build can be set to show a prompt asking whether to reverse a partially approved transaction instead of continuing (Reversal prompt for partial approval, under the Misc. tab).
entries.quote: You can enable the option “Reversal prompt for partial approval” under the Misc. tab in the file build.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Remove or force the PIN prompt
steps: The terminal cannot force a PIN prompt: the card-issuing bank decides whether a PIN is required.
PIN bypass can be set in the file build (EMV tab) to User Bypass, Auto Bypass or Disabled.
entries.quote: We cannot force the PIN to prompt on transactions as it is up to the card issuing bank whether the PIN is required for that transaction or not.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Cannot void a transaction
steps: A void only works while the transaction is in the current open batch.
If the batch has been closed, process a Refund/Return instead.
To void: choose the transaction type Credit/Debit.
Select V/Sale.
Enter the transaction number.
Confirm or press Enter.
A receipt confirming the void prints.
entries.quote: Choose transaction type Credit/Debit -> Select V/Sale -> Enter the transaction number -> Confirm or press Enter -> a receipt confirming the Void will be printed.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Surcharge fee is not applied to a card
steps: Surcharge applies only to credit transactions made with a true credit card.
The chip reader identifies the card: if it has a Debit AID, no surcharge is applied.
entries.quote: If it identifies that the card has Debit AID, no surcharge fee will be applied to the credit transaction.

steps: PAX refers transaction and batch inquiries to the processor.
entries.quote: For Transaction/Batch Inquiry

entries.quote: Please contact your SIM Card Provider

entries.title: Warranty on PAX products
steps: Warranty details vary.

entries.title: Email a receipt to the customer
steps: PAX payment applications do not email receipts.
Emailing depends on a third-party POS application in or connected to the terminal.
entries.quote: PAX payment applications do not email receipts.

entries.title: Debit, EBT, FSA, HSA or eWIC
steps: Debit and EBT can be processed on an encrypted terminal.
FSA, HSA or eWIC payments work only when the terminal is attached to a POS that can send the authorization information for those payments.
entries.quote: You can process Debit or EBT on an encrypted terminal.

entries.title: Sales tax on the terminal
steps: Sales tax is calculated separately on a point of sale, which sends the total to the payment application.
Some applications support a prompt for tax in the transaction; the tax then prints on the receipt and on the batch report.
entries.quote: Some applications support having a prompt for tax in the transaction.

entries.title: Connection options on a PAX Android terminal
steps: All PAX Android devices support Wireless and Wi-Fi.
LAN, dial or Bluetooth depend on the model's specifications or accessories.
entries.quote: All PAX Android devices support Wireless and Wi-Fi.

entries.title: PAX repair (RMA) and warranty check
steps: PAX offers a warranty status check and a Return Material Authorization (RMA) repair request.
The request asks for the terminal number, the serial number and a description of the issue.
entries.quote: Check on your warranty status or request a Return Material Authorization (RMA) repair.

entries.title: Prepare the battery before first use (remove the white tab)
steps: Open the battery cover on the bottom of the terminal.
Take out the battery.
Find the white tab on the battery and peel it back carefully until it is fully removed and the POGO pins are visible.
entries.quote: Locate the white tab on the battery and peel back carefully until it is fully removed and the POGO pins are visible.

entries.title: Swipe a magnetic stripe card
steps: Slide the card through the reader slot, left to right or right to left, with the magnetic stripe facing the body of the device.
Make sure the card is fully in the reader while swiping.
entries.quote: Slide the card through the card reader slot from left to right or from right to left with the magnetic strip oriented towards the body of the device.

entries.title: Insert a chip card
steps: Insert the card fully into the reader with the metallic contacts facing up and towards the device.
Make sure the card is fully inserted.
entries.quote: Insert the card fully into the reader with the metallic contacts facing up and towards the device.

entries.title: Tap a contactless card or phone
steps: Hold the card or device roughly within an inch of the contactless reader.
For best results hold it as close as possible and centred over the indicated area.
entries.quote: The contactless card reader reads cards and devices placed roughly within an inch (2.5 mm). For best results, place as close to the reader as possible and center the card over the indicated area

entries.title: Clean the device
steps: Do not use industrial strength or abrasive cleaner; it may damage or scratch the screen.
Do not immerse the device in water or liquid.
Do not spray water or cleaner into the card reader or ports.
To clean the screen, put distilled water or mild glass cleaner on a soft, lint-free cloth and wipe gently.
entries.quote: To clean the screen, apply distilled water or mild glass cleaner onto a soft, lint-free cloth and gently wipe terminal.

entries.title: Battery is deformed or damaged
steps: Stop using the battery immediately.
Replace it.
entries.quote: If the battery is deformed or damaged, please stop using immediately and replace it.

entries.title: Battery lasts only half as long as when new
steps: If the working time is only half that of a new battery, the battery may be at the end of its life.
Replace the battery.
entries.quote: If the continuous working time is only half of a new battery, the battery life may be at its end. Please replace it.

entries.title: Battery charging rules
steps: Do not charge for more than 24 hours at a time.
If the battery is out of power, recharge it and then disconnect the device.
Recharge the battery at least once every 6 months.
Replace the battery every two years.
Use only the specified battery model and charger.
entries.quote: The charging time cannot exceed 24 hours. If the battery is out of power, please recharge in an appropriate time and then disconnect the device.

steps: Press and hold the power button for about 3 to 5 seconds until the shutdown menu appears.

Gently slide the tray back in.

Replace the cover.

Insert the communication cable head into the Type-C interface.

entries.title: Fit and activate a SIM card (A920 Pro)
steps: Slide the latch on the back to the right and lift off the battery cover.
Lift the battery out from the bottom.
Place the mini-SIM card into the SIM1 slot (usually the left one).
Put the battery back and secure the cover.
Hold the power button for 2 to 4 seconds to turn the terminal on.
Go to Settings.
Select Wireless & Networks or Cellular Settings.
Make sure Mobile Data is turned on.
A cellular signal icon shows in the top header once active.
entries.quote: Place the mini-SIM card into the SIM1 slot (usually the left one) as indicated

entries.title: Connect the A920 Pro over LTE/4G/3G (set the APN)
steps: Open the Settings app, outside of the BroadPOS app.
Enter the password; the default is pax9876@@ (or 9876).
Select Network & Internet.
Select Mobile Network.
Expand Advanced.
Select Access Point Names.
Under Name, change the setting to Broadband.
Under APN, change the setting to Broadband.
entries.quote: Open the Settings app (Outside of the Broadpos app)
entries.note: 'Broadband' is the APN for the SIMs Paysafe ships (matches the AT&T fix in our sheets); the right APN depends on the SIM provider. Source names BroadPOS.

entries.title: Connect the A920 Pro to Wi-Fi
steps: Select the Settings app on the idle screen.
Enter the Settings password, select the green check button and select OK.
Turn Wi-Fi on.
Select the network.
Enter the Wi-Fi password and select connect.
entries.quote: Input the Settings password, then select the green check button and select OK.

entries.title: Wi-Fi network is not in the list (A920 Pro)
steps: In the Wi-Fi screen select the 3 dots in the top right corner.
Select Add Network.
Enter the network name (SSID) and select the security type.
Enter the Wi-Fi password and select Save.
entries.quote: If the desired Wi-Fi network is not displayed, select the 3 dots in the top right-hand corner, then select Add Network.

entries.title: Change the paper roll (A920 Pro)
steps: Turn the device over.
Pull the paper cover latch away from the device; the top section pivots down.
Pull the old roll out.
Insert the new roll with the paper poking out of the top of the device, in the orientation shown in the holder.
Close the lid until it snaps into place and is fully closed.
Tear off any excess paper.
entries.quote: To install a new thermal paper roll, insert the paper roll with the paper poking out of the top of the device, adhering to the orientation shown in the paper roll holder.

entries.title: Power the A920 Pro on
steps: Press and hold the power button for three seconds until the screen powers on.
entries.quote: Press and hold the power button for three seconds until the screen powers on.
entries.note: PAX's own guide says 3 to 5 seconds.

entries.title: Power the A920 Pro off
steps: Press and hold the power button for three seconds until the power menu shows.
Tap Power off.
Tap Power off again; a 'shutting down' message shows.
entries.quote: Press and hold the power button for three seconds until the power menu is shown.

entries.title: Sleep or wake the A920 Pro
steps: Click the power button once to put the device to sleep or wake it.
entries.quote: To put the device in or wake the device from sleep mode, click the power button.

entries.title: Run a sale (A920 Pro, Paysafe build)
steps: From the main menu choose Sale.
Key in the amount and select Done.
When prompted to Tap, Swipe or Insert, have the customer tap on the contactless reader, swipe through the magstripe reader or insert into the card reader.
entries.quote: Key in the amount of the sale and select Done.
entries.note: Paysafe help-centre article for Paysafe's own build; the application is not named and its menu (Sale / Refund / Admin) may differ from BroadPOS on our terminals.

entries.title: Run a refund (A920 Pro, Paysafe build)
steps: From the main menu choose Refund.
Key in the refund amount and select Done.
When prompted, have the customer tap, swipe or insert the card.
entries.quote: Key in the amount of the refund and select Done.
entries.note: Paysafe help-centre article for Paysafe's own build; the application is not named and its menu may differ from BroadPOS on our terminals.

entries.title: Print an X report / end of shift (A920 Pro, Paysafe build)
steps: From the main menu swipe across to the Admin menu.
Choose X Report (End of Shift).
The report prints; an X report can be taken at any time and does not zero the totals.
entries.quote: An X report can be taken at any time of the day and does not zero totals.
entries.note: Paysafe help-centre article for Paysafe's own build; the Admin menu / X Report is not the BroadPOS FUNC > Reports layout.

entries.title: No Paper Mode message (Paysafe steps)
steps: Open the paper compartment and place the roll thermal side down.
If No Paper Mode still shows, select FUNC, then Settings.
Enter today's date as the password.
Select Operation Settings.
Select No Paper Mode.
Select settings.
Switch to Auto Check.
entries.quote: Open the paper compartment and place the roll (thermal side down)
entries.note: Paysafe article for 'my PAX terminal' (FUNC menu = BroadPOS-style app). PAX's own FAQ says to choose 'Auto'.

entries.title: Invalid batch sequence error (A80, Paysafe steps)
steps: It usually means a mismatch, often an open batch from the previous day or a problem at batch close.
Try closing the batch manually: FUNC, BATCH, BATCH CLOSE.
Check the Ethernet or Wi-Fi connection.
If one transaction is the problem: void it if unsettled, refund it if settled.
Other fixes in the source (clear the batch under System Settings > Database; change the Device ID or batch number) are for support.
entries.quote: Force Batch Close: Try closing the batch manually via the FUNC menu (FUNC > BATCH > BATCH CLOSE).
entries.note: PAX's own FAQ fixes this by raising the batch number by 1 under Function > Settings > Host settings. Clearing the batch deletes transactions, so we route it to tech.

entries.title: Terminal freezes or crashes
steps: Hold down the power button until the terminal powers off.
Wait a few seconds, then press the power button again to restart.
Make sure the device is charged or plugged in; if it uses a charging base, check the base is connected to power.
If it still happens, check the internet connection (Wi-Fi, Ethernet or cellular) and reconnect or restart the network.
If the terminal has a built-in printer, open the lid and check for a paper jam or misfeed.
If restarting does not fix it, contact support with the terminal model, a description of the issue and any error messages on the screen.
entries.quote: Hold down the power button until the terminal powers off.
entries.note: General Paysafe article for all terminal brands, not PAX-specific.
